entity.summary: Seychelles-registered centralized cryptocurrency exchange operating since 2018 and offering spot and derivatives markets through its active global platform.
entity.notes: Official company material and an independent exchange profile support the 2018 operating year and continuing service. On 2026-09-27, an attacker used an API key that remained on a previously compromised user account after account recovery to transfer funds before the incident was fully contained. MEXC CEO Vugar Usi later said the user was fully compensated. HEI treats this as an account-level security incident rather than a platform-wide wallet compromise; MEXC remains active.

expected.summary: Seychelles-based centralized exchange launched in 2018 and still operating under the MEXC brand.
expected.notes: Official MEXC materials state that the exchange has operated since 2018.

events.title: MEXC began operating
events.description: MEXC began operating as a centralized cryptocurrency exchange in 2018.
events.notes: Year-level launch marker because the official company page states the operating year without an exact public day.

events.title: Hong Kong's SFC warned against unlicensed MEXC activity
events.description: Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission warned that MEXC was actively promoting virtual-asset trading services to Hong Kong investors without a licence application and added it to the Suspicious Virtual Asset Trading Platforms Alert List.
events.notes: The warning was jurisdiction-specific and did not establish a global shutdown or alter MEXC's active entity status.

events.title: MEXC confirmed unauthorized withdrawals through a residual API key
events.description: MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said a compromised user account had been frozen and restored, but an API key that remained on the account allowed the attacker to transfer funds before the incident was fully contained. MEXC later fully compensated the affected user. Independent reporting based on the user's account put the withdrawals at roughly USD 340,000.
events.notes: This was an account-level compromise, not a confirmed platform-wide hot-wallet breach or smart-contract exploit. Public reports differ by timezone on whether the withdrawal sequence falls on September 26 or 27; HEI uses 2026-09-27 for the incident marker. The affected user alleged forged/AI-generated identity material was used during the account takeover, but MEXC's public confirmation established the residual API-key mechanism and compensation, not the alleged KYC-bypass method, so HEI does not present the deepfake claim as a confirmed platform finding.

evidence.title: MEXC Confirms $340,000 Loss From API Key, Fully Compensates Affected User
evidence.notes: Independent report reproducing MEXC CEO Vugar Usi's confirmation that a residual API key remained after account recovery, enabled the transfer, and that MEXC fully compensated the affected user. It also reports the affected user's asset amounts and account-takeover timeline.

evidence.title: MEXC CEO stated that the residual API key caused funds to be transferred out and has fully compensated
evidence.notes: Independent report summarizing the CEO statement: MEXC detected abnormal account activity, froze the account, helped restore the original email and authenticator, later found that a residual API key enabled the transfer, and provided full compensation while investigation continued.

evidence.title: MEXC User Alleges $340,000 Loss After Attacker API Was Not Revoked
evidence.notes: Contemporary report based on the affected user's disclosure, including approximately 322,110 USDT and 9,133,999 ONE withdrawn after the account-recovery process. Used for the reported amount and sequence, not as sole proof of the attacker's identity-verification method.
